text: Refines D-0364 for #675, at @gitdek's request that the charts integrate with the dashboard without making the page asymmetrical, and his idea of a chart that shows on hover and opens its details on click. The dashboard shows projects as one row per model instead of a grid of cards: projects whose models are identical share the row, with a chip for each implementation linking its own evidence page. Each row starts with a tile of one size. A checked chart's tile frames the top of its poster, shows the poster whole beside it while a mouse rests on it or it has keyboard focus, and opens the evidence page on click; a tap opens the page. A model with no reader chart says why in its tile, with its checked state count, and the tile opens its evidence page; as D-0353 has it, no raw graph stands in for a reader chart, and TLC's raw state graph stays the separately labeled detail. The dashboard links no standalone SVG, which isn't readable on its own; the evidence page still links the complete image. The table view lists one line per project, its number cells no longer styled as the page's number tiles. Presentation only: no evidence, URL or identity changes, so a deploy restores the cached snapshot.
